title: 03 — ML Engineer Track
html:
03 — ML Engineer Track

The one idea: an ML engineer makes models useful and safe in production. That takes data engineering skill (features, pipelines), modelling skill (training, evaluation) and operations skill (serving, monitoring). Learn them in that order, building every method once by hand before using a library.

1. Level 1: Foundation

Read, in order Why
Data Engineer Track, Level 1 Models are only as good as their data
AI & ML Foundations The map of the field
Training and Evaluation from Scratch How training works, and how to evaluate honestly
Statistics for Data Quality and Drift Distributions, outliers, drift

Project: logistic regression written by hand (numpy) on a public or made-up dataset, then the same with scikit-learn. Report AUC, precision and recall at a chosen threshold, and a calibration table.

Checklist:

  • I can derive the logistic-regression gradient and explain each term.
  • I split before any preprocessing, and can explain why.
  • I can explain why accuracy fails on rare events.

2. Level 2: Practitioner

Read, in order Hands-on
Features and Feature Stores Point-in-time training set with merge_asof
Trees, Boosting and Tuning LightGBM or XGBoost with early stopping and Optuna
Time Series Forecasting and Nowcasting Walk-forward backtest against seasonal naive
Entity Matching Probabilistic matching as an ML problem
The Databricks AI Stack, sections on MLflow Track every run

Project: a downgrade-risk or fund-flow model on made-up data, with point-in-time features from a bitemporal table, tuned boosting, a walk-forward backtest, and every run tracked in MLflow.

Checklist:

  • My training set provably uses no future information.
  • My model beats a simple baseline on an untouched test or out-of-time set.
  • Every result can be reproduced from a run id.

3. Level 3: Professional

Read, in order Hands-on
MLOps on Databricks End to End Unity Catalog registry with aliases, batch scoring job, monitoring job
Credit Risk Modelling A scorecard with WoE, IV, Gini, KS and reason codes
Neural Networks and Transformers from Scratch Backprop by hand, then PyTorch
LLM Engineering & RAG Retrieval with citations, evaluation
Document Intelligence Extraction with confidence and a review queue

Project: a production-shaped model. Champion and challenger aliases, a promotion rule with per-segment checks, batch and real-time scoring, inference logging, and a PSI monitor that opens a retraining task.

Checklist:

  • Promotion is a rule plus a named approval, not a manual copy.
  • I can tell input drift, output drift and performance decay apart, and I monitor all three.
  • Every score row records the model version and the data vintage.

4. Level 4: Senior

Read Focus
Fine-Tuning and LoRA When to fine-tune, and how to prove it helped
Securing Agents and MCP Tools Safety of LLM systems
Personal Data and DPDP Privacy in training and inference
Graphs and Knowledge Graphs Network features and context for agents
  • Model risk: inventory, independent validation, documentation and periodic review.
  • Platform: shared feature store, evaluation harness, serving standards, cost per prediction.
  • Leadership: decide build vs buy vs fine-tune, and set the evaluation bar for the team.

Checklist:

  • I have shipped a fine-tuned or distilled model that beat the prompted baseline on a frozen set.
  • Our models have documented limits, owners and review dates.
  • I can defend each model's cost, risk and value to a non-technical committee.
